name: CQL++
tagline: 1990s C++ SQL database with ODBC, embedded SQL and an ISAM layer, later released as free source code.
description: CQL++ is an ANSI SQL-89 database management system with ODBC extensions from Machine Independent Software Corporation, distributed with complete C++ source code. It is layered so programmers can work at several levels: the ODBC API (Level 1 plus parts of Level 2), an SQL API used by a preprocessor for embedded EXEC SQL statements, and lower ISAM and B+tree layers for direct record access. It shipped as a single-user library with full COMMIT/ROLLBACK and crash recovery, and as a client/server version providing repeatable-read isolation for multiple users. The client/server code was later made available free of charge, first under the GPL and then under a looser custom license. The site is now maintained in memory of its author Seth Kurtzberg, copyright ends in 2010, and the newest download is a 10.0 beta.
statusNote: No development since about 2010; the site is kept online in memory of its author and paid support is unavailable.

pricing.notes: Source free to download; paid support is no longer offered.

strengths: Complete C++ source for a small SQL engine with ODBC, embedded SQL and ISAM layers
Transactions with crash recovery in both single-user and client/server builds
Lets code drop down to ISAM/B+tree access when SQL is too heavy
weaknesses: Unmaintained since about 2010, with builds tied to old compilers
useCases: Studying the internals of a compact SQL engine
Maintaining legacy applications built on it
notIdealFor: Modern SQL features or concurrency needs
